_jestCompatIsolationFiles: 2026-10-01: the hot runtime's RNTL hook registration (native/rntl-hooks.mjs) and the jest-compat caller lookup (jest-compat/caller.mjs) each add a shipped runtime file. _floors: Floors exist because every limit here used to be a ceiling, so the check passed on an unbuilt tree (files: 8) and on a build missing the verbatim-copied native runtime (files: 60) — neither of which can run a test. They sit roughly 10% under the current artifact (re-baselined alongside the ceilings, 2026-09-01): far enough not to churn on ordinary changes, close enough that losing a build entry or the native runtime trips them.
_ceilings: Roughly 5% above the current artifact (312520 packed, 1051250 unpacked, 86 files as of 2026-09-30), deliberately. This re-baseline combines the runtime ownership architecture (ownership policy, bounded hot memory, state manifest, isolated registry compilation) with main's requireActual alias hand-off, which together exceeded the file ceiling (86 / 85) and left 1.4% byte headroom. Raise a ceiling only with a measured artifact and a recorded reason; never move it just past the current size.
_warnHeadroomRatio: A ceiling that is about to be exhausted should say so while there is still room to act. The check prints remaining headroom for each bounded scale budget and warns below this ratio, so re-baselining is a deliberate act taken with notice rather than a fix applied after main has gone red — which is how the last two raises actually happened, both times from changes that were green individually. Warnings are limited to the scale budgets: maxRuntimeDependencies is a policy cap where sitting at the limit is the intended state, and exportPaths is exact, so neither has headroom to report.
_exportPaths: Exact, not a ceiling. 11 since ./rntl-matchers: a types-only entry that augments Vitest's Assertion with React Native Testing Library's matchers. It is separate rather than folded into the main types because RNTL is an optional peer, and an unresolvable type import inside a shipped .d.ts reports TS2307 for consumers using skipLibCheck: false without it. Removing an entry is a breaking change for consumers and adding one is a support commitment, so both require editing this number.
